method: Per-venue-class research workstreams, each independently searched and required to cite a fetched URL for every capacity figure and calendar URL. Compiled deterministically; identity reconciled conservatively; nothing admitted to any production registry.

workstreams.method_notes: Independent cross-check of two never-verified census populations (INDOOR_ARENA n=41; GREYHOUND_STADIUM n=18, all 18 capacity-review-flagged) plus the arena-adjacent sporting populations (ice hockey, basketball, athletics, tennis). Existing census venues were extracted programmatically from research/major-event-venues/uk-major-event-census-01/venues.json (642 venues; 41 INDOOR_ARENA, 18 GREYHOUND_STADIUM, 14 OTHER_SPORTS_VENUE) and every candidate below was name+city+alternative-name matched against the full 642 before being proposed, so nothing here is a known duplicate. REFERENCE POPULATIONS CHECKED: (1) National Arenas Association member list (fetched https://www.nationalarenasassociation.com/ - 23 members incl. one Irish); (2) Wikipedia List of indoor arenas in the United Kingdom (operational, under-construction and former sections); (3) Elite Ice Hockey League 2025-26 season venue list (10 venues); (4) Super League Basketball 2025-26 season venue list (9 venues); (5) Greyhound Board of Great Britain's own published licensed-track count (fetched https://www.gbgb.org.uk/racing/race-courses/ and https://www.gbgb.org.uk/rules-regulation/licensing/tracks/ - BOTH state 16 licensed stadia) cross-read against the named 16-track list and then confirmed track-by-track against each track's own official site; (6) UK greyhound openings/closures register maintained by the trade publication Greyhound Racing Times; (7) major permanent tennis tournament venues; (8) major athletics stadium population. VERDICT - INDOOR_ARENA: UNDERCOUNTED. The top-tier concert/entertainment arena estate is in fact substantially covered by the census as a whole - every NAA member arena except one, and every operational arena on the Wikipedia UK indoor arena list, reconciles to an existing census record - but several of them sit under a DIFFERENT venue_type and so are excluded from the 41 (P&J Live Aberdeen is CONVENTION_CENTRE; Brighton Centre, Swansea Building Society Arena, Alexandra Palace and Windsor Hall/Bournemouth are AUDITORIUM; Olympia London and The NEC are EXHIBITION_CENTRE; Royal Albert Hall is CONCERT_HALL; Emirates Arena Glasgow is OTHER_SPORTS_VENUE). Those are classification questions, not gaps, and are reported rather than re-listed here so as not to create duplicates. The REAL undercount is in the mid-scale (1,400-3,500 capacity) purpose-built sporting/entertainment arena tier: only 2 of the 9 Super League Basketball venues (Copper Box Arena, Playsport Arena) were in the census at all, and 1 of the 10 EIHL venues (Planet Ice Altrincham) was missing. Six operational arena-type venues and one under-construction arena are added below, plus one genuinely missing NAA member arena (East of England Arena, Peterborough) classified as MULTI_PURPOSE_EVENT_COMPLEX. VERDICT - GREYHOUND_STADIUM: MATERIALLY WRONG, NOT MERELY INCOMPLETE. GBGB itself states 16 licensed tracks; the census carries 18 active ones. Both surplus records are corrected below: Oxford Stadium closed on 3 April 2026 and is set CLOSED; Mildenhall Stadium's greyhound operation closed on 2 April 2026 while the site itself continues as a Spedeworth speedway/stock-car venue, so it is re-typed OTHER_SPORTS_VENUE and left OPERATIONAL rather than being falsely killed off or falsely preserved as an active track. All 18 existing greyhound records are re-listed (same canonical_name + city) because all 18 carried CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED and six carried no official URL at all; this pass supplies verified official URLs, addresses and fixture calendars. VERDICT - ICE HOCKEY: PLAUSIBLY_COMPLETE after one addition (9 of 10 EIHL venues already present). VERDICT - BASKETBALL: UNDERCOUNTED (5 of 9 top-tier venues added; 2 more fall below the 1,000 threshold and are excluded with cited figures). VERDICT - ATHLETICS: PLAUSIBLY_COMPLETE - Alexander Stadium, London Stadium, Manchester Regional Arena, Gateshead International Stadium, Crystal Palace NSC, Scotstoun Stadium, Cardiff International Sports Stadium and the indoor Emirates/Glasgow International Arena are all already in the census; no >=1,000 athletics venue was established as missing. VERDICT - TENNIS: UNDERCOUNTED BY ONE - AELTC, Queen's Club, Devonshire Park and Nottingham Tennis Centre were present; Edgbaston Priory Club (Lexus Birmingham Open) was not and is added. EXCLUSIONS ARE STATED EXPLICITLY in each excluded venue's absence and in the report: Surrey Sports Park (970), SGS College/WISE Arena Bristol (750) and Lee Valley Athletics Centre (500 permanent seats) are all below the 1,000 threshold; Dundonald International Ice Bowl is a public leisure ice rink and Belfast Giants training/secondary venue with no established spectator capacity; Edinburgh Arena at Edinburgh Park has planning consent but construction had NOT started as of July 2026, so no permitted operational_status honestly applies and it is deliberately omitted; the remaining Planet Ice community rinks (Blackburn, Bristol, Gillingham, Gosport, Hemel Hempstead, Leeds, Peterborough, Solihull, Uttoxeter, Widnes) were not evidenced as >=1,000 major-event infrastructure and are omitted. NO capacity, address, postcode, date or URL below is asserted without a URL that was actually fetched; where no figure was found the capacity is null with CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED rather than guessed. Latitude/longitude are null throughout by instruction.

Breadth-first census of UK concert halls, theatres and auditoria with capacity >= 1,000 across all four nations, compiled 2026-09-20 from pages actually fetched in-session. Most capacities are GRADE_B (Wikipedia article wikitext retrieved via the MediaWiki API; the exact API URL fetched is cited as capacity_source), with GRADE_A first-party confirmation where a venue or operator site could be fetched (e.g. Usher Hall 2,200 from cultureedinburgh.com, Sheffield City Hall operator from sheffieldcityhall.co.uk). Roughly 22 candidate venues were verified to be under 1,000 and excluded: 19 West End houses (Ambassadors 444, Apollo 658, Arts 350, Criterion 588, Duchess 494, Fortune 432, Garrick 718, Gielgud 994, Harold Pinter 796, Lyric 915, Noel Coward 942, Playhouse 550, @sohoplace 602, St Martin’s 550, Theatre Royal Haymarket 888, Tom Stoppard 640, Trafalgar 630, Vaudeville 690, Wyndham’s 799) plus Eden Court Empire Theatre 840, Dundee Rep c.455 and Theatr Clwyd 570; numerous sub-1,000 studio/second spaces inside included complexes (Lilian Baylis 200, Sage Two 600, Barbican Pit 200, Lyttelton 890, Dorfman 400, Spa Theatre 675, Sheffield Memorial Hall 500 and others) are noted in capacity_configuration rather than listed separately. Known limitations: several official sites (royalalberthall.com, southbankcentre.co.uk, lwtheatres.co.uk, trafalgarentertainment.com) returned 403/404/bot-detection so no first-party evidence was obtained for them; capacities marked CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED are venues confirmed to exist on a fetched operator directory but whose size was not verified, and Theatre Royal Brighton in particular may prove sub-1,000 on review. St David’s Hall Cardiff is recorded with operational_status STATUS_REVIEW_REQUIRED rather than OPERATIONAL because the fetched Wikipedia article states it closed in September 2023 due to RAAC in the roof and was "not expected to reopen until 2026" — whether it has now reopened was not verified.

Every capacity figure, square-metre figure, address and URL recorded below was read from a page that was actually fetched during this research pass; figures that appeared only in search-engine result summaries were deliberately NOT recorded, and those fields are left null with capacity_confidence CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED. Official first-party venue sites were preferred (GRADE_A); no third-party venue-directory figures were used as a capacity source. Calendar sources were only recorded where a fetched page listed actual forthcoming NAMED events; venues whose only public page was a 'hire our venue' / event-types marketing page were given zero calendar_sources and a no_public_calendar_reason. Operators were recorded only where a fetched page stated them, so several are null rather than guessed.

Dedicated second-pass national census of UK major business-event infrastructure, run because the first pass admitted only 22 conference/convention/exhibition venues (10 CONVENTION_CENTRE + 12 EXHIBITION_CENTRE, and CONFERENCE_CENTRE zero times). METHOD: (1) The 642 existing census records in venues.json were read programmatically and reduced to a canonical_name+city+nation+venue_type index; every candidate below was checked against that index before research, so venues already carried by other workstreams (e.g. Winter Gardens Blackpool, Venue Cymru, Westpoint Exeter, Brangwyn Hall, Caird Hall, Glasgow Royal Concert Hall, Music Hall Aberdeen, Usher Hall, Ulster Hall, Millennium Forum, Donald Gordon Theatre, The Glasshouse International Centre for Music, Brighton Dome, St George's Hall Bradford, Butterworth Hall, Bolton Arena, Silverstone Circuit) were deliberately NOT re-listed. (2) POPULATIONS ACTUALLY CHECKED, deliberately overlapping and never treated as truth on their own: Association of Event Venues full member directory (aev.org.uk/about-us/venue-members, 56 records across 6 pages, fetched); London & Partners / London Convention Bureau conference-venues directory (conventionbureau.london, all 6 pages); Unique Venues of London full member list (uniquevenuesoflondon.co.uk); Convention Edinburgh / Meeting Edinburgh searchable venue directory (meetingedinburgh.com/venues, 114 records with Max Theatre / Reception / Banqueting columns); Glasgow Life venue-hire directory (glasgowlife.org.uk/venue-hire, 3 pages); VisitScotland Business Events (businessevents.visitscotland.com - venue directory path is 404; only the conferences-and-exhibitions inspiration page carries capacities); VisitAberdeenshire business events (business.visitabdn.com - names no venues, lead-capture only); Business Events Wales / Meet in Wales (meetinwales.com - /venues is 404 and the search is client-rendered, but individual product pages carry structured capacity fields); Visit Cardiff / Meet Cardiff (meetcardiff.com/venues and /highlights/ pages); Visit Belfast business events (visitbelfastbusiness.events - client-rendered, static HTML exposes only 4 featured listings and its sitemap contains no venue pages: a genuine unswept population); NewcastleGateshead Convention Bureau; the agricultural-society / county-showground estate reached venue-by-venue from official society sites; and the official venue websites themselves, which were the primary evidence source throughout. (3) EVIDENCE RULE APPLIED: every non-null capacity_value cites the exact URL fetched that states it. Where a venue publishes only floor area, or only standing figures, or nothing, that is recorded honestly rather than guessed - six records carry capacity_value null with CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED. No coordinates were guessed; latitude/longitude are null throughout. Addresses and postcodes appear only where a fetched page stated them. (4) CALENDAR RULE APPLIED: venue-hire pages, capacity charts and floor plans were NOT recorded as calendars. Only pages listing actual named forthcoming events were recorded, and events_currently_present is true only where named forthcoming events with dates were actually seen in the fetched page. (5) CONSISTENT EXCLUSION RULE: hotel-integrated ballrooms and function suites were excluded even at 1,000+ (InterContinental London - The O2 / Arora Ballroom 3,100 theatre; JW Marriott Grosvenor House Great Room 1,300 theatre; Novotel London West Champagne Suite 1,400 theatre; Hilton Birmingham Metropole; Celtic Manor Resort Caernarfon Suite 1,200 theatre; Macdonald Aviemore Resort Osprey Arena 1,150 theatre; Prestonfield Edinburgh 1,000 theatre). These are evidenced and named in the hand-back report so the census owner can reverse that judgement in one pass. (6) LIMITATION: the session's WebSearch budget (200 calls) was exhausted partway through, so later discovery was WebFetch-only, navigating from official sites. Several sites refused automated fetches entirely (c-h-w.com, eastsiderooms.com, qub.ac.uk, swansea.gov.uk, ulster.ac.uk, visitpeterborough.com, cardiff.ac.uk) - where a figure could still be obtained it is marked with its real source grade, and where it could not, the gap is stated rather than filled.

Breadth-first census built entirely from pages fetched during this task: four Wikipedia stadium lists (England, Scotland, Wales-by-capacity, Northern Ireland) plus the 2026-27 Cymru Premier and NIFL Premiership club/ground tables were downloaded as rendered HTML and parsed mechanically (rowspans resolved, capacity templates expanded), so every name, capacity and city here was read from a real table cell rather than recalled. Coordinates, street addresses and official-website URLs came from the Wikidata API keyed on those articles' enwiki titles; 407 resulting official club/venue homepages were then fetched (357 returned 200) and every calendar URL recorded below was extracted from that fetched HTML, never guessed, then itself fetched (355 of 360 returned 200). Manchester City refused the bulk probe with HTTP 403 and was re-fetched by hand, so the Etihad Stadium entry is evidenced the same way as the rest. Coverage: all four nations, the top four English tiers plus National League/North/South grounds above ~5,000, every Scottish ground at or above 1,000, all NIFL Premiership and Cymru Premier grounds, and the national stadiums. Limitations to read honestly: capacity is almost entirely GRADE_C (Wikipedia tables, sometimes corroborated by Wikidata P1083) because the official club and stadium pages checked - Wembley, Hampden, Windsor Park, Old Trafford, Spurs, Etihad, Emirates, Ibrox, Wrexham - publish no capacity figure in fetchable HTML; only Swansea.com Stadium yielded a GRADE_A official figure. Where two fetched sources disagree (notably NIFL's current licensed capacities vs the NI stadium list) the current-season club table was preferred and the conflict is recorded with capacity_confidence LOW. events_currently_present is a mechanical signal (schema.org Event blocks or date-like strings in the fetched HTML), left null where a page returned 200 but was client-rendered. Murrayfield Stadium and Kingston Park appear in football-stadium source lists but were excluded because every tenant evidenced is a rugby organisation; Principality Stadium is included because the brief names it, flagged in its evidence as having no football use evidenced. Non-football venues in the Welsh general stadium list (rugby, cricket, ice hockey) were excluded. Only "Current stadiums" sections were used, so no closed or under-construction grounds are listed.

Breadth-first census of UK indoor arenas with capacity >= 1,000 across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, compiled 2026-09-20 from live WebSearch/WebFetch only. Population was seeded from the Wikipedia 'List of indoor arenas in the United Kingdom' (which only covers >= 5,000) and then extended downward using the Elite Ice Hockey League arena table, Planet Ice / council leisure operators, and convention-centre operators to reach the 1,000-9,999 band. Capacity figures are graded honestly: GRADE_A means the figure was read off a page on the venue's or operator's own site that I fetched; GRADE_C means a Wikipedia infobox or a WebSearch result summary. Where two sources disagree (common, because arenas have concert / sport / half-house configurations) the principal figure is in `capacity` and the rest in `additional_capacities`, with the conflict noted; where nothing could be verified the capacity is null and flagged CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED. Every URL in this file was returned by a search or fetch performed in this session - none are recalled from memory. This is research only: no source registry or public data was touched.

Targeted national pass for UK performance venues with capacity >= 1,000, run 2026-09-20 against the existing 642-venue census. RECONCILIATION: research/major-event-venues/uk-major-event-census-01/venues.json was parsed programmatically (never eyeballed) and every existing canonical_name + alternative_names + city combination was extracted before any candidate was written. The file grew from 642 to 676 records while this pass was running, so the de-duplication was re-run against the final 676-record state across ALL venue_types (not just performance types) using normalised name matching that strips punctuation, case and a leading definite article. That second pass caught four candidates already present under conference/multi-purpose classifications - Central Hall Westminster (London), Tobacco Dock (London), Edinburgh Corn Exchange (Edinburgh) and McEwan Hall (Edinburgh) - and they were removed from this file rather than duplicated. No venue in this file collides with any existing census record on name+city. OPERATOR PORTFOLIOS CHECKED AND RECONCILED LINE BY LINE: ATG Entertainment (full UK list via en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ambassador_Theatre_Group - ALL 33 UK venues already in the census, zero gaps); Trafalgar Entertainment / former HQ Theatres (19 UK venues via en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trafalgar_Entertainment - 6 gaps found and added: Congress Theatre, Winter Garden Eastbourne, G Live, Fareham Live, Pavilion Theatre Glasgow, Bradford Live); Nimax Theatres (only the Palace Theatre is >= 1,000 and it is already present); LW Theatres / Really Useful Group (all six >= 1,000 houses already present); Delfont Mackintosh (all six >= 1,000 houses already present); Nederlander UK (Adelphi, Aldwych, Dominion all present); Academy Music Group (full venue table via en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Music_Group - 10 gaps >= 1,000 added; O2 Academy Glasgow, O2 Shepherd’s Bush Empire and Newcastle City Hall were already present); AEG (The Halls Wolverhampton added; The O2, OVO Arena Wembley, Eventim Apollo already present; indigo at The O2 added as a distinct room); NEC Group (NEC, ICC, Symphony Hall, Utilita Arena Birmingham, bp pulse LIVE all present); ASM Global / Sheffield Theatres / Birmingham Hippodrome / Capital Theatres / Bradford Theatres (no >= 1,000 gaps found). POPULATIONS SWEPT: (a) en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_End_theatre full capacity table - every West End house at or above 1,000 seats was already in the census, so the suspected West End gap does not exist; (b) the complete "Indoor theatres and halls" table of en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_venues_in_the_United_Kingdom read as raw wikitext and filtered to >= 1,000; (c) a Wikidata SPARQL capacity query (P1083 >= 1000, P131* within England/Scotland/Wales/Northern Ireland) returning 864 rows, of which 86 distinct performance-venue-typed records were cross-checked; (d) MediaWiki revisions-API retrieval of 210 individual venue articles for infobox capacity, address, owner and operator; (e) 230 direct fetches of official venue and local-authority sites for first-party capacity and what’s-on pages. LARGE LOCAL-AUTHORITY ESTATES CHECKED: Croydon, Watford, St Albans, Tunbridge Wells, Eastbourne, Hastings, Bexhill (Rother), Wolverhampton, Blackburn with Darwen, Preston, Warrington, Carlisle, Middlesbrough, Kirklees, Calderdale, North Lincolnshire, East Lindsey, Harrogate/North Yorkshire, Scarborough, Cornwall, BCP/Poole, Portsmouth, Guildford, Fareham, Peterborough, Glasgow Life, City of Edinburgh, Aberdeen City, Stirling, Renfrewshire, Denbighshire, Belfast. NATIONS: Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland were swept deliberately and separately rather than as a by-product of a London/England sweep. CAPACITY RULE APPLIED: the principal capacity_value is always a single main auditorium, never a sum of a building’s rooms; secondary rooms go to additional_capacities. Where a venue is admitted on a standing rather than seated configuration (Alban Arena, Engine Shed, Exeter Great Hall) that is stated explicitly in capacity_configuration. DELIBERATE EXCLUSIONS ON EVIDENCE: Royal Hall Harrogate was investigated and EXCLUDED because the official Harrogate Convention Centre venue page states a theatre capacity of 978, below the 1,000 threshold. O2 Academy Edinburgh was EXCLUDED because its AMG slug returned HTTP 404 when probed live, indicating it is no longer an operating AMG venue, despite appearing in the AMG Wikipedia table at 3,000. Sub-1,000 houses confirmed and skipped include Gielgud (994), Noel Coward (942), Lyric Shaftesbury Avenue (915), Wyndham’s (799), Theatre Royal Haymarket (888), Sheffield Crucible (980), Orchard Theatre Dartford (956), Churchill Theatre Bromley (785), Devonshire Park Theatre (873), Cheltenham Town Hall (978), Weymouth Pavilion (988) and Queen’s Hall Edinburgh (801). HONEST NULLS: seven venues are recorded with capacity_value null and capacity_confidence CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED (Hall for Cornwall, Huddersfield Town Hall, Parr Hall, The Sands Centre, Albert Halls Stirling, Paisley Town Hall, Rhyl Pavilion Theatre) because no fetched page stated a figure. They are NOT asserted to meet the >= 1,000 threshold. SHARED CALENDAR PLATFORMS RECORDED: academymusicgroup.com/<venue-slug>/events (11 live slugs confirmed by live HTTP probe; pattern opened in a real browser at O2 Academy Brixton and confirmed to render named dated events); trafalgartickets.com/<venue-slug>/en-GB (4 venues here, covering 5 auditoria); betterboxoffice.co.uk/<venue-slug> (GLL/Better); everyonetheatres.com/theatres/<venue-slug>/ (Everyone Active); bwdvenues.com (Blackburn with Darwen, multi-venue); boxoffice.middlesbrough.gov.uk (Middlesbrough, multi-venue); glasgowlife.org.uk/whats-on/glasgow-life-tickets (Glasgow Life, multi-venue); scunthorpetheatres.co.uk (North Lincolnshire, multi-venue); eastbournetheatres.co.uk via trafalgartickets (multi-venue).

Breadth-first census compiled 2026-09-20 from live fetches of operator, venue and governing-body sites, with Wikipedia used only where a first-party figure was unavailable (marked GRADE_B). The 59-course British racecourse list was taken from the Wikipedia List of British racecourses table and cross-checked against the RCA/BHA count (Jockey Club 14, ARC 16, 27 independent); Down Royal and Downpatrick were added for Northern Ireland, giving 61 racecourses. Racecourses, circuits and greyhound stadiums almost never publish a single spectator capacity, so capacity_value is null and capacity_confidence is CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED for the large majority; where a venue stated an attendance band or licensed figure (Taunton 10,000 licensed; Salisbury 2,000-9,000; Chester 20,000+ per race day; Fakenham 1,500-4,500+; Epsom 28,000+ on Derby Day) that wording is preserved verbatim in scale_description rather than converted into a number. Three operators share one site platform each, which matters for ingestion: Jockey Club Racecourses (thejockeyclub.co.uk/<course>/events-tickets/, verified on Cheltenham, Aintree, Epsom, Newmarket, Haydock, Sandown), Arena Racing Company (per-course domains with /whats-on and /popular-events/live-music, verified on Doncaster and Chepstow) and MotorSport Vision (per-circuit domains with /calendar, verified on Brands Hatch, Donington, Oulton Park, Snetterton, Cadwell Park). Where a sibling venue site was not individually fetched, the calendar_sources note says so explicitly.

Breadth-first census built entirely from pages fetched live on 2026-09-20 via WebFetch/WebSearch: three Wikipedia capacity-list pages (rugby union stadiums, rugby league stadiums, cricket grounds by capacity) for population discovery, then per-venue Wikipedia infobox fetches for capacity, address, owner/operator and coordinates, then official venue sites for first-party calendar/event URLs. No capacity, URL, coordinate or venue name in this file was written from model memory: every figure traces to an 'evidence' entry naming a URL that was actually fetched. Authority grading is honest — GRADE_A means the venue's own site stated it, GRADE_B a per-venue Wikipedia infobox, GRADE_C an aggregate list page or a search-result summary. Known limitations: (1) coordinates and first-party calendar URLs are missing for most Championship-level rugby league grounds and several smaller county cricket grounds, because the time-box was spent on breadth rather than depth; (2) the Wikipedia rugby union list page is visibly stale (it still shows pre-rename stadium names and pre-2023 Premiership membership), so venues sourced only from it carry LOW confidence; (3) Stormont (Northern Ireland cricket) is included with a null capacity pending direct verification; (4) concert/conference calendar sources were only captured where a fetched official page actually exposed them.

SPORT_COMPLETENESS_AUDIT_02 - audit of the SPORTING estate of the UK major-event venue census (census baseline 642 venues). Scope covered: rugby union, rugby league, cricket, horse racing, motorsport, and a systematic-gap spot-audit of football. Indoor arenas, greyhound, ice hockey, basketball, athletics and tennis were OUT OF SCOPE for this workstream (handled separately) and were deliberately not worked on.

THIS FILE CONTAINS 92 RECORDS: 80 NEW VENUES and 12 CORRECTION RECORDS. New venues break down as 36 rugby union grounds, 22 cricket grounds, 9 motorsport venues (5 circuits + 4 speed hillclimbs), 7 rugby league grounds and 6 football stadiums. 0 racecourses were added - horse racing was audited and found genuinely complete. Every correction record deliberately reuses the census's EXACT existing canonical_name and city so it reconciles onto the record it corrects, and asserts no capacity unless it is correcting one.

=== PER-SPORT AUTHORITATIVE POPULATIONS CHECKED, AND VERDICTS ===

1) HORSE RACING - VERDICT: PLAUSIBLY_COMPLETE. Population checked: the operating Great Britain racecourse estate (via greatbritishracing.com/racecourses/, which reports 59 results, and the Wikipedia List of British racecourses, which states 59 operating in Great Britain as of 17 September 2026), plus Northern Ireland's two courses, plus the two operator portfolios (thejockeyclub.co.uk lists 14 racecourses; arenaracingcompany.co.uk/racing/horse-racing/our-racecourses lists 16). Expected population 59 GB + 2 NI = 61. Census had 61. ADDED 0. The census's 59 GB courses were diffed name-by-name against the authoritative 59 and match EXACTLY. Both operator attributions also reconcile exactly: the census's 14 Jockey Club courses and 16 ARC courses match the operators' own published portfolios. NO CLOSED COURSE IS WRONGLY RETAINED - Folkestone (last raced 18 December 2012) and Towcester (closed 2018) are both correctly absent, and Hereford, which closed in 2012 and reopened in 2016, is correctly present as OPERATIONAL. This sport needed correction in neither direction.

2) MOTORSPORT - VERDICT: UNDERCOUNTED. Population checked: the Motorsport UK / operator-portfolio permanent circuit estate (msv.com, barc.net/about/, motorsportuk.org, motorsportni.org). EXPECTED_POPULATION_UNKNOWN - no governing body publishes a definitive count of licensed permanent circuits with public spectator calendars. Census had 14. ADDED 9 (5 circuits: Mallory Park, Lydden Hill, Kirkistown, Three Sisters, Crail Raceway; plus 4 speed hillclimbs: Shelsley Walsh, Prescott, Harewood, Gurston Down). The most material gap is KIRKISTOWN - the census contained NO Northern Irish motorsport circuit at all. Rockingham Motor Speedway (closed 24 November 2018) and Arena Essex/Lakeside (last meeting 4 November 2018) were verified closed and are correctly ABSENT from the census, so no closed circuit is wrongly retained. Bedford Autodrome was examined and deliberately EXCLUDED: MSV operate it, but its own site shows it is a PalmerSport corporate/track-day venue "with no requirement for crowd-protecting safety barriers", i.e. not a public spectator race facility. Blyton Park and Teesside Autodrome were excluded on the same basis.

3) RUGBY UNION - VERDICT: UNDERCOUNTED, and the census was a SEASON OUT OF DATE. Populations checked: PREM Rugby (premrugby.com/clubs/, 10 clubs); Champ Rugby, English tier 2 (the RFU-operated champrugby.com plus the 2026-27 Champ Rugby teams-and-stadia table, 14 clubs); the URC's UK clubs; and the Welsh and Scottish club estates via the two unions' own shared fixture platforms (my.wru.wales/fixtures-results and fixtures.scottishrugby.org/club-rugby). Census had 40 RUGBY_STADIUM records (covering both codes). ADDED 36 rugby union venues - 13 in England (Champ Rugby), 1 PREM Rugby, 13 in Wales and 9 in Scotland. Findings: (a) PREM Rugby - exactly ONE gap, StoneX Stadium (Saracens); the other nine clubs' grounds were all present, several under FOOTBALL_STADIUM (Ashton Gate, Principality). (b) URC - COMPLETE; all seven UK clubs' grounds present. (c) Champ Rugby - 10 of 14 grounds missing. CRITICAL: the obvious source (the 2025-26 season table) is STALE - Cambridge and London Scottish have been relegated out, and Blackheath (Well Hall) and Rotherham Titans (Clifton Lane) promoted in; Coventry's ground was renamed from Butts Park Arena to the Nick Newbold Stadium with effect from 21 March 2026. The 2026-27 table was used instead. (d) WALES - 11 major grounds >= 1,000 missing, including Newport Stadium, which a NAME COLLISION was hiding: it is Newport RFC's actual regular home since October 2021 and is a DIFFERENT venue from Rodney Parade, which the census already held. (e) SCOTLAND - 8 grounds missing, including The Greenyards (home of the Melrose Sevens) and Raeburn Place (site of the first rugby international, 27 March 1871).

4) RUGBY LEAGUE - VERDICT: UNDERCOUNTED. Population checked: superleague.co.uk/clubs (14 clubs, 12 UK after excluding Catalans Dragons and Toulouse Olympique) and the 2026 Betfred Championship (rugby-league.com plus the 2026 RFL Championship article). STRUCTURAL FINDING: RFL LEAGUE 1 NO LONGER EXISTS for 2026 - rugby-league.com states "Following confirmation of a merger of the Championship and League 1 competitions at the end of last season, 2026 will include 21 teams", reduced to 20 after Featherstone Rovers were removed following December 2025 administration. So the expected population is 12 UK Super League grounds + 20 Championship grounds. ADDED 7 grounds (Steel City Stadium, South Leeds Stadium, Morson Stadium, Stadiwm Eirias, Victoria Pleasure Grounds, Crow Trees Ground, Avery Fields). All 12 UK Super League grounds were already present.

5) CRICKET - VERDICT: UNDERCOUNTED, materially. Populations checked: the 18 first-class county headquarters; the county outground/festival estate via each county's own grounds pages (Kent, Surrey, Sussex, Middlesex, Lancashire, Derbyshire, Yorkshire, Gloucestershire, Worcestershire); Cricket Scotland and the Wikipedia list of cricket grounds in Scotland; and Cricket Ireland's international grounds. The census's 20 comprise all 18 first-class county HQs plus Stormont and The Grange - i.e. the HQ layer was complete but the ENTIRE non-HQ layer was missing. ADDED 22 cricket grounds. Highlights: North Marine Road Scarborough (the principal English outground), Arundel Castle (a genuine international venue with the richest outground calendar found anywhere in this audit), and AO FARINGTON - Lancashire CCC's purpose-built SECOND HOME, opened 2026 on a 250-year lease, which is the most significant new non-HQ cricket venue in the UK. Scotland went from 1 cricket ground to 5 (Mannofield Park Aberdeen is larger than The Grange by the cited figures); Northern Ireland from 1 to 4.

6) FOOTBALL (spot-audit for systematic gaps only - the long tail was deliberately NOT ground through) - VERDICT: the top tiers are NEARLY complete but contain one severe classification gap. === EVIDENCE-QUALITY CAVEATS, STATED HONESTLY ===
 - SEASONAL TIMING: today is 2026-09-20. The 2026 rugby league season has FINISHED and the English cricket season is in its final week, so many first-party calendars legitimately show no forthcoming fixtures. Every such case is recorded events_currently_present:false with the reason stated - this reflects calendar timing, not an absent calendar, and these sources are worth re-checking in November/December 2026.
 - NO OFFICIAL CAPACITY EXISTS FOR WHOLE CLASSES OF VENUE. Established as a systematic finding, not an excuse: no county club or ECB page states a capacity for ANY non-headquarters cricket ground; no Champ Rugby club site states a capacity for any of the 13 grounds checked; and neither the WRU nor Scottish Rugby publishes ground capacities. Those capacities are therefore GRADE_C/LOW by necessity and must not be laundered into club-sourced facts.
 - HONEST NULLS: 25 records carry capacity_value null with capacity_confidence CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED. 16 of those are new venues where no number could honestly be cited, and each carries documented scale facts instead: all 5 new circuits, all 4 hillclimbs, The Greenyards and Myreside (sources conflicting by more than an order of magnitude), The Lamb Ground, Crow Trees Ground, Avery Fields, AO Farington and College Ground Cheltenham. Two of those 16 (Crow Trees Ground, Avery Fields) carry an EXPLICIT REVIEWER WARNING that the 1,000 threshold is NOT established on cited evidence and that a reviewer may legitimately reject them. The other 9 nulls are correction records that deliberately assert no capacity so the census's existing figure is left untouched.
 - NO RECORD IN THIS FILE CARRIES A CAPACITY BELOW THE 1,000 THRESHOLD. Where a documented figure fell below it - K-Park Training Academy (700) and AO Farington's official 700 fixed seats - it is reported in prose or in additional_capacities and was NOT used as a principal capacity.
